title: Tracker Core Investigations
mission: Scan public Epstein records and convert them into tracker-ready records, tasks, institution lanes, source routes and proof boundaries.
boundary: Each scan item records what an official or reputable source route shows. It does not infer guilt, relationship type, passenger identity, private victim identity, or wrongdoing beyond the record text.

batches.title: Epstein File Scan Batch 001 — DOJ Library Structure And Court-Record Lanes
batches.summary: First defensive scan of the official DOJ Epstein Library and DOJ Disclosures page. This batch builds source-route records rather than allegations: DOJ library warnings, data set structure, court-record lanes, FOIA lanes, prior disclosures, the January 30 production statement, and three high-priority court-record pages.

records.title: DOJ Epstein Library — privacy and search boundary
records.evidenceGrade: A for official source-route and boundary statement
records.recordShows: The DOJ Epstein Library is the official library for materials responsive under the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The page warns that the library may include sensitive or non-public personal information despite redaction efforts, gives a correction email route, notes sexual-assault content, and warns that search may be unreliable for handwritten or poorly formatted materials.
records.recordDoesNotShow: It does not verify the content of any individual file or make any named-person allegation.
records.nextPull: Add a privacy-warning banner to every Epstein scan page and avoid victim identifiers, private personal data and unsupported claims.
records.confidenceImpact: A for source route and privacy/search boundary.

records.title: DOJ Disclosures — Data Sets 1 through 12
records.evidenceGrade: A for index existence; C for individual file content until opened
records.recordShows: The DOJ Disclosures page lists Data Sets 1 through 12 with separate file pages.
records.recordDoesNotShow: It does not classify the documents inside those data sets or prove the content of any individual PDF without review.
records.nextPull: Create a dataset-by-dataset scan queue beginning with Data Set 9 and record first-page file IDs for batch tracking.

records.title: DOJ Court Records — consolidated case lane
records.recordShows: The DOJ page states that court records from the former Court Records page were consolidated and lists multiple court-record pages, including Doe cases, State of Florida v. Epstein, United States v. Epstein, United States v. Maxwell, Government of the USVI v. JPMorgan Chase Bank, and estate/probate-related matters.
records.recordDoesNotShow: It does not summarize each case outcome, allegation, finding, settlement, or docket event without opening the individual record pages and PDFs.
records.nextPull: Create separate case cards for United States v. Epstein, United States v. Maxwell, State of Florida v. Epstein, USVI v. JPMorgan, and Estate of Epstein.
records.confidenceImpact: A for case-lane existence; C for case-specific interpretation.

records.recordDoesNotShow: It does not classify specific CBP/FBI/BOP/Florida documents without file-level review.
records.nextPull: Open each FOIA category and create sub-tasks for transport/logistics, federal investigation records, custody/death records, and Florida public-records materials.
records.confidenceImpact: A for route; C for file content.

records.recordShows: The DOJ page lists prior DOJ disclosure routes: First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files, BOP Video Footage, Maxwell Proffer, and Memoranda and Correspondence.
records.recordDoesNotShow: It does not verify the substance of any prior disclosure without opening the linked pages/files.
records.nextPull: Create a prior-disclosures scan batch focused on custody/death records, proffer records and correspondence lanes.

records.title: DOJ January 30 production statement — 3 million additional pages and production limits
records.evidenceGrade: A for DOJ production statement; C for any file-level interpretation
records.recordShows: The DOJ stated on January 30, 2026 that it published over 3 million additional responsive pages, more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images; combined with prior releases, nearly 3.5 million pages. DOJ also stated collection sources included Florida and New York Epstein cases, the New York Maxwell case, New York death-investigation cases, a Florida case involving a former Epstein butler, multiple FBI investigations and the OIG investigation into Epstein’s death. It also warned that public submissions may include fake or falsely submitted material.
records.recordDoesNotShow: It does not verify every published file as true, complete or probative, and DOJ itself warns some produced public-submission material may be fake or false.
records.nextPull: Add a fake/false-material warning to Evidence Policy and require file-level verification before claims are upgraded.
records.confidenceImpact: A for production scope and limitations; C/X review needed for individual public-submission claims.

records.confidenceImpact: A for case page; C for allegations or compliance conclusions until file-level review.
